dimensions.assessment: Affects incumbent long-term lessees of federal property within National Park System units.
dimensions.evidence: the lessee entered into the lease not less than 5 years before

dimensions.assessment: Allows lease extensions without competitive bidding, directly altering contract terms for qualifying incumbent operators.
dimensions.evidence: extend a lease... without issuing a request for bids or a request for proposals

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative lease management rather than direct federal appropriations or revenue adjustments.
Modifies agency lease regulations and creates a narrow exception to standard competitive bidding requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Secretary of the Interior shall revise part 18 of title 36, Code of Federal Regulations

dimensions.assessment: Affects lease terms up to the cumulative limits permitted under existing regulations.
dimensions.evidence: cumulative length of such lease complies with part 18 of title 36

missing_information: Exact count of National Park Service leases meeting the 5-year requirement
Estimated economic value of the non-competitive lease extensions
importance_detail.rationale: The bill permits the National Park Service to grant a single non-competitive lease extension for qualifying long-term lessees under specific administrative determinations. The reach is confined to existing park leaseholders meeting the five-year tenure requirement.
